method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A' (published 5 October 2021). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC8862646). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Spasticity is raised muscle tone caused by an upper motor neurone lesion.** Brain causes include stroke, acute brain injury and cerebral palsy; spinal causes include multiple sclerosis and spinal cord injury.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Drug treatment is only for disabling spasticity**: spasticity that the patient or their carers feel is getting in the way of body function, activities or participation. Spasticity that causes no problem should not be treated with drugs, but any grade, mild to severe, can become disabling.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Why it matters:** spasticity commonly brings pain, poor sleep, feeding problems and difficulty with positioning, transfers, dressing and self-care. Treatment aims to protect function and to prevent contractures and skin breakdown.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start with a multidisciplinary physical management programme**, led by physiotherapy and occupational therapy: posture, positioning with equipment and splints, stretching and standing.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Look for and treat anything that is driving the spasticity**, such as bladder or bowel problems and damaged skin.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral antispasticity drugs are usually tried first**, but they often fail or cause side effects. The next step is then botulinum toxin type A (BoNT A) or intrathecal baclofen (ITB).
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The distribution of spasticity drives the choice.** Focal or segmental disabling spasticity is best treated with BoNT (98.7% consensus). Multi-segmental or generalised disabling spasticity that has not responded to oral drugs is best treated with ITB (96.1% consensus).
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Multi-focal spasticity** (non-adjacent joints, such as ankle and hip, or wrist and shoulder) was also placed in the BoNT arm; the advisory board was unanimous.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lower limbs only:** ITB is **not** recommended when only one leg is affected (87.0% negative consensus); that is focal or segmental disease, so use BoNT with walking aids, splints and rehabilitation, partly because ITB may weaken the unaffected side. When both legs are affected, ITB is a good option (97.4%), and when both legs plus back or abdominal muscles are affected, all respondents agreed (100%).
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Arms and legs together:** when both sides are affected, ITB is the treatment of choice. When one side is affected (hemiplegia), ITB is supported only weakly and BoNT alone may also help.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Arms only, both sides:** BoNT rather than ITB. One arm alone falls in the focal arm, where BoNT is also first choice.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Combine ITB with BoNT** in generalised or multi-segmental spasticity when ITB alone does not meet the patient's goals (over 75% agreement). If arm goals are unmet after starting ITB, add BoNT early for the arms.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After BoNT, ITB is a second-line option** (90.9% consensus) when rehabilitation goals are still unmet after a trial of oral medication.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **What tips the choice towards ITB:** the benefit-risk balance (84%), whether the patient will adhere to treatment (79%), BoNT needs reaching the maximum recommended dose (77%), and the patient's goals and expectations (76%).
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ITB is delivered by an implanted programmable pump and catheter**, using under 1% of the oral dose directly at the spinal cord. Its best-proven effect is on leg spasticity of cerebral or spinal origin after maximum tolerated or recommended oral antispasmodics have failed.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ITB acts less on the arms and trunk:** roughly one-third of its leg effect, more at higher doses and depending on where the catheter tip sits.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Before ITB, the patient, family and carers must be engaged and willing** to have a test-dose trial, the implant operation, and regular follow-up for pump refills.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **ITB has a relatively high complication rate:** infection, cerebrospinal fluid leak and catheter problems in particular.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Walking does not rule out ITB.** It has traditionally been kept for people who cannot walk, but early ITB may help people keep walking for longer, particularly in progressive disease such as multiple sclerosis. That group has more catheter complications.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BoNT dose limits constrain widespread spasticity.** Multi-focal or multi-segmental treatment may need more toxin per session than the licensed doses, and higher doses raise concern about systemic spread and neutralising antibodies.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start BoNT early:** most experts give it straight away (31.2%) or within 3 months of disabling spasticity starting (49.4%), to prevent secondary complications.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **ITB is usually started later** (at least 4–6 months, or over 6 months), but that delay is inappropriate when the patient is losing range of movement, especially with dysautonomia after brain injury, where ITB helps.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure outcomes:** the Ashworth or modified Ashworth scale for tone and spasms, the visual analogue scale or Numeric Pain Rating Scale for pain, the Barthel Index for function, and the Goal Attainment Scale for goals.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use shared decision-making at every step**, taking patient and carer preferences into account (96.1% agreed). The algorithm supports clinical judgement; it does not replace it.
claims.locator: European expert advisory board (8 specialists, survey of 77 experts from 17 countries), Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine vol 54, doi 10.2340/16501977-2877, 'European expert consensus on improving patient selection for the management of disabling spasticity with intrathecal baclofen and/or botulinum toxin type A', published 5 October 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862646/, retrieved 2026-09-23
